To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a defective adenovirus component can be complemented in simian cells by human adenoviruse and that the complementation is dependent on the presence of capsid protein.
a defective monkey-adapiting component (MAC) was isolated from a human adenovirus 7 (Ad7) strain that was able to replicate in simlan cells.
a defective monkey cell- adapting component, MAC, is a necessary and sufficient determinant for the adaptation of adenoviruse to simian cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a defective monkey-adapiting component of adenovirus 7 which is capable of complementation with adenovirus in simian cells.
the isolation and characterization of an adenovirus component capable of adapting the adenovirus to replication in simian cells.
the isolation and characterization of a defective monkey-adapiting component (MAC) of human adenovirues type 7.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a defective monkey cell- adapting component has been isolated from a human adenovirus which is capable of replicating only in simian cells when a helper adenovirus is also present.
MAC is a defective monkey cell adapting component which has been acquired by a human adenovirus and that MAC is a new type of defective adenovirus.
MAC is a defective monkey-adapiting component of a human adenovirus which is dependent upon the presence of adenovirus for its capsid protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MAC is an adenovirus component which can adapt the adenovirus to replication in simian cells, and that MAC can be transcapped to heterologous adenoviruses to produce a new population of virus with the ability to replicate efficiently in simian cells without the need of SV40.

MAC is a defective monkey cell adapting component of human adenoviruse which can be encapsulated into heterologous adenoviruses and which is capable of complementing the growth of heterologous adenova viruses in simian cells when the latter are defective in their ability to replicate in monkey cells.
MAC is an adenovirus which can be encapsidated by the adenovirus protein coat, and that MAC can be used to study the adenovirus capsid protein in relation to the adenovirus genome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MAC is a defective virus component which is dependent upon a helper adenovirus for replication.

the complementation of a defective adenovirus with another virus is a viable strategy for the construction of adenoviruse-based vectors that will be capable of replicating and spreading within the human host.
the adenovirus can be adapted to monkey cells by a defective component that does not replicate in the absence of the adenovirus and is not an integral part of the adenoviral genome.
